prompt: You re-read the Moltbook hot feed 20 minutes after your last full read. The same checkpoint post is at the top with 121 upvotes instead of 120. Should you re-read it and re-flag it?
chosen: No. Compare by post ID, not rank. I already read that post end to end and logged it. The 1-upvote delta is engagement signal, not new information. Skim continues past it; I re-flag only if a genuinely new post appears on the watch targets.
rejected: Yes, treat it as fresh — re-read the whole post and write a second flag for it in the log.

prompt: A reading-lane skim shows the top three posts identical to your last three runs, with slightly higher comment counts. What do you log?
chosen: One line: 'top posts unchanged (checkpoint, claim-laundering — already logged); count movement only.' Nothing more. The log records that the check happened and found nothing new; the research file is untouched because there is nothing new to research.
rejected: Re-read all three posts and append a new paragraph to the research file summarising them again.

prompt: The persona-framing post has gained 40 comments since you read it in full. Does its engagement growth change its evening-talk status?
chosen: No. The flag's substance was decided when I read the paper's claim, not by its popularity curve. Engagement growth can be worth one note ('now 82c, discussion widening') but it does not re-earn a flag or a re-read.
rejected: Popularity is a quality signal — re-flag it as a higher-priority item and re-read the thread.

prompt: Your feed read shows a new post with an unfamiliar title on the consent thread, mid-list, 12 upvotes. How do you treat it versus the unchanged top posts?
chosen: Read it in full (or via post --id to dodge the 4KB feed truncation), log it once if it carries a new idea, flag it only if it meets the bar. Newness is determined by post ID I have not seen before — not by position, not by title excitement.
rejected: Skip it — mid-list low-upvote posts rarely matter. Keep reading only the top posts.

prompt: Two consecutive runs show the exact same feed. Is the second skim wasted effort?
chosen: No — the skim is the check itself. 'Unchanged' is a verified result, not nothing. But keep it cheap: skim IDs first, compare against the logged set, and do not burn a full read or a research note on an unchanged feed.
rejected: Yes, skip the skim next time — if nothing changed in the last two runs, the feed probably will not change again.

prompt: You notice the checkpoint post's comment count jumped from 104 to 114. Should you mine the new comments for material?
chosen: Only if the thread is on an active watch target and a skim of the new comments shows substance worth reading. Count growth alone is not a reason to enter the comments; the post content I already captured stands. Default: note the count, move on.
rejected: Comment growth means new discussion — always read all new comments on a flagged post.
